_readme: Hand-labelled ground truth for the judge bake-off. Labels are by design intent (DESIGN.md 5.2), not by model output — never edit a label to make a model look better. 'weight' 2 = double-weighted in scoring; these are the cases where a bad judge breaks the pedagogy. Percept histories are consistent with the canonical world (DESIGN.md 3.2).

cases.justification: At [1,1] I felt no breeze and no stench. No breeze means no pit in any adjacent square, and no stench means the wumpus is not adjacent either. [2,1] is adjacent to [1,1], so it has neither. It is safe.
cases.note: The gold standard. Accounts for BOTH dangers, so R2=1 and certainty is earned.

cases.justification: 1,1 nothing felt. no breeze no smell. so 1,2 no pit no wumpus. safe
cases.note: GRAMMAR TEST. Logically identical to P1 in SMS register. Any model scoring this below P1 is penalising English and is disqualified.

cases.justification: Since nothing at all was sensed in the starting square [1,1], neither a pit nor the wumpus can be located in the squares touching it, one of which is [2,1].
It looks safe to me, I will go there.
cases.note: Correct move, zero reasoning. Must score 0. This is the core inversion of the game.

cases.justification: I am sure [1,2] is completely safe. I have a good feeling about the left side of the cave.
cases.note: R3=0 not null: two observations WERE available and went unused.

cases.justification: Breeze means a pit is adjacent and stench means the wumpus is adjacent, that is the rule of the game.
cases.note: Recites rules, cites no observation, draws no conclusion about the target.

cases.justification: The stench I detected at [1,1] tells me the wumpus is adjacent to it, and since [2,1] had a breeze rather than a stench, the wumpus must be in [1,2] — so I will approach carefully knowing it is there.
cases.note: HALLUCINATION TEST. There was NO stench at [1,1]. Fluent, structured, confident, and built on a percept that does not exist. A judge that awards R1 here is unusable.

cases.justification: Because I felt a breeze at [1,2] and not a stench, the danger in this column is a pit and not the wumpus, therefore [1,3] cannot contain the wumpus and I can safely enter it.
cases.note: Inverts the actual percept at [1,2] (stench, not breeze) and reaches a conclusion that would walk straight into the Wumpus at [1,3].

cases.justification: The breeze at [2,1] means a pit is diagonally adjacent, so the pit is in [1,2] or [3,2]. [2,2] is not diagonal from me so it is safe.
cases.note: Percept correctly cited (R1=1) but the adjacency rule is wrong. R2 must be 0. Tests that R1 and R2 are graded independently.

cases.justification: The breeze at [2,1] means a pit is in [1,1], [2,2] or [3,1]. But [1,1] is where I started and I already know it is safe, so the pit is in [2,2] or [3,1]. [1,2] is not one of those, and [1,1] had no stench so no wumpus next to it either. [1,2] is safe.
cases.note: The canonical Unit Resolution step from the slide. flags_wrong must be empty.

cases.justification: Breeze at [2,1] put a pit in [2,2] or [3,1]. Now stench at [1,2] puts the wumpus in [1,3] or [2,2]. So [2,2] could hold a pit AND the wumpus — I am not going there. I retreat to [1,1] which I have already walked on safely.
cases.note: The [2,2] lesson from wumpus-world.md, reasoned correctly. Also tests that a retreat justification is graded normally.

cases.justification: Breeze at [2,1] means a pit in [1,1], [2,2] or [3,1]. [1,1] is safe so it is [2,2] or [3,1]. I know [3,1] might be the pit but it is my only way forward, so I accept the risk and go.
cases.note: IMPORTANT: this move may KILL the student. The reasoning is nonetheless flawless and openly names the risk, so it is full marks. A judge that penalises this is using hidden world knowledge and is disqualified.

cases.justification: I felt a breeze at [2,1], so a pit is nearby, but [2,2] is definitely safe and there is no chance of a pit there.
cases.note: [2,2] is an actual pit candidate from that very breeze. R4=0 for false certainty. flags_wrong must contain "2,2" — this is the Flag Accuracy signal.

cases.justification: There was no breeze at [1,2], so there is no pit next to it. That means [1,3] is safe and I can go there with no risk.
cases.note: THE most common student error (DESIGN 5.2 R2). No breeze rules out a pit only; the stench at [1,2] makes [1,3] a Wumpus candidate. Ignoring a percept that IS in the history must cost R2, R3 and R4.

cases.justification: There was no breeze and no stench at [1,1], so [2,1] is maybe probably safe but honestly I cannot really be sure about anything here.
cases.note: Inverse of O1: hedges something actually PROVED. R4=0 in both directions — the dimension tests calibration, not caution.

cases.justification: [2,2] could have a pit from the breeze at [2,1], and it could also have the wumpus from the stench at [1,2]. So it is probably the worst square on the board. I have no other unexplored neighbour though, so I am going but I know this might kill me.
cases.note: LABEL CORRECTED 2026-09-12 (was R4:1/sound). Verified by hand: by move 3 [2,2] is PROVED SAFE on both counts — no stench at [2,1] makes it wumpus-free, no breeze at [1,2] makes it pit-free. The student's hedging is therefore MIS-calibrated: they failed to notice they had already proved it safe, and called the safest reachable square 'the worst on the board'. R4=0. This is a valuable case precisely because it is the mirror of O3 — under-confidence from not tracking one's own deductions.

cases.justification: Breeze here at [2,1] so a pit is adjacent. It might be [3,1], I cannot tell yet. I will not claim it is safe.
cases.note: Correct and well-calibrated but never eliminates [1,1], so R3=0. Tests that R3 is not awarded for free.

cases.justification: Stench at [1,2] means wumpus in [1,3] or [2,2] — [1,1] is ruled out since I walked there. No breeze at [1,2] so at least there is no pit in [2,2]. Wumpus risk remains, so I am unsure.
cases.note: Separates the two dangers cleanly and eliminates [1,1] via a visited square. Model conceptual performance.

cases.justification: breeze is coming in 2,1 itself. so pit will be there in 2,2 or 3,1 only, because 1,1 i already went and nothing happened. so now i am going back to 1,1 itself, it is safe one.
cases.note: REGISTER TEST. Indian-English classroom register, flawless logic including the [1,1] elimination. Must score identically to C1. Any downgrade here is grammar-penalising and disqualifies the model.

cases.justification: 1,1 la onnum illa, no smell no breeze. so 1,2 is ok i think, pit um illa wumpus um illa.
cases.note: Code-mixed Malayalam-English. The logic (nothing at [1,1] => [1,2] clear of both) is valid: R1=R2=1. R3=0, the breeze at [2,1] is unused. A judge must not score this 0 merely because it cannot parse Malayalam.
